  "decisions": [
    {
      "id": "D1",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-02",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Use gray-matter + remark/rehype (data-driven) instead of mdsvex-as-routes for content parsing/rendering.",
      "rationale": "Posts are pure content, not interactive Svelte templates; avoids mdsvex's known limitation where a +layout.svelte can't directly read a child .md file's frontmatter; keeps frontmatter access uniform everywhere (listings, post pages, RSS, sitemap) via one loader function.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "mdsvex-as-routes",
        "MDX-flavored starters (e.g. sveltekit-blog-mdx)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D2",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-02",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Static prerendering via adapter-static, not SSR.",
      "rationale": "No runtime backend needed; output is a plain static folder deployable anywhere. Tag/pagination routes must stay crawlable or be listed explicitly in config.kit.prerender.entries.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Default SvelteKit SSR"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D3",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-02",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Core/site split (filepress core engine + independent Site repos) is a first-class requirement from the start, not a later refactor.",
      "rationale": "SvelteKit's routing/build system is inherently per-project (hard framework constraint) — every Site must be its own SvelteKit project. Core centralizes content loader, markdown pipeline, feed/sitemap generators, shared layout/theme components, and scaffolding.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Single monolithic project serving multiple blogs via config (not possible under SvelteKit)",
        "Copy-paste the engine per site"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D4",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-02",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Sites depend on filepress core via a pinned git URL dependency (tag/commit), not a main-floating or npm-published dependency.",
      "rationale": "Avoids needing to publish/maintain a public npm package while still allowing normal package-manager installs; pinning means a core change never silently changes a site's next build without a deliberate version bump. Superseded 2026-08-11 by publishing npm package getfilepress while retaining git-pin install path for CI.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Publish core to npm under a scoped name (deferred, not needed for v1)",
        "Floating dependency on main"
      ],
      "status": "superseded",
      "superseded_by": "D14"
    },
    {
      "id": "D5",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-04",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Deploy to Cloudflare Pages, always on a custom domain from day one.",
      "rationale": "CF Pages has native git integration to build adapter-static output on push to main. A custom domain means the site is served at root, so adapter-static needs no base-path/subpath configuration.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "GitHub Pages (would need base-path config unless on a custom domain)",
        "Netlify",
        "Vercel"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D6",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-04",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Post content lives in a top-level /posts/ directory, outside src/.",
      "rationale": "Easier to find and edit via the GitHub mobile app's file browser since it is not nested inside app source.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "src/content/posts/"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D7",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-04",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Drafts (draft: true) are excluded from index, tag pages, RSS, and sitemap, but still built at their normal /posts/<slug> URL (unlinked) for private preview.",
      "rationale": "Lets the owner preview formatting on a phone before flipping draft: false, without exposing the post in any discoverable listing or feed.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Fully exclude drafts from build output entirely"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D8",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-04",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Dates are strict YYYY-MM-DD only; future-dated posts are hidden until their date arrives.",
      "rationale": "One accepted date format keeps sorting unambiguous and lets malformed dates fail loudly (naming the file). Future-dating uses a build-time 'date <= today' check tied to the CI run's date so scheduled posts stay hidden until the next build on/after that date.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Accept full ISO datetime strings",
        "Include future-dated posts immediately"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D9",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-04",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Visual direction is sparse, sharp/classic, high-end and uncluttered; core supports selectable per-site themes that are all variations on this shared aesthetic.",
      "rationale": "Restrained editorial typography and minimal chrome fit a text-first blog and keep client JS minimal (Lighthouse 95+ goal). Selectable themes give per-site variety without each site diverging into a wholly different design, so most theme code stays in core.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Bare-minimum default typography only",
        "One fixed shared theme with no per-site selection",
        "Fully independent per-site designs"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D10",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-04",
      "phase": "1-architecture",
      "decision": "Core versioning is informal (pin sites to core commit SHAs as needed); the scaffold command is a local script run from the core repo, not a published CLI.",
      "rationale": "Fastest path for v1 with a single maintainer and no public distribution; a semver release process and an npx CLI can be added later if multiple sites make change-tracking painful. Superseded in spirit by Option D published CLI bins on getfilepress (still informal engine versioning / git pins).",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Semver-tagged core releases from the start",
        "Published npx filepress create CLI"
      ],
      "status": "superseded",
      "superseded_by": "D14"
    },
    {
      "id": "D11",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-05",
      "phase": "4-feature-iteration",
      "decision": "Default theme is 'Essay' — a quiet, text-first editorial look (Ben Evans / Stratechery family) with self-hosted Newsreader (reading serif) + Inter (UI/meta), a single accent used at three intensities (strong / rule / wash), and warm parchment neutrals with a dark variant.",
      "rationale": "the quiet single-column serif look serves reading and keeps client JS ~zero (Lighthouse 95+ goal, D9). Fonts are bundled via @fontsource-variable so there are no third-party font requests. Design is expressed as CSS custom properties so per-site theme variants (D9) stay cheap.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Warmer editorial/journal (Traveling Mitch)",
        "Magazine card grid (Copyblogger)",
        "System-font stack only (no font files)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D12",
      "timestamp": "2026-07-05",
      "phase": "4-feature-iteration",
      "decision": "First feature batch: excerpt post cards, featured latest post + index pagination (/page/[n]), optional per-post author byline, prev/next post links, a config-driven Topics/Explore view, a config-driven external newsletter CTA, and image-only paragraphs becoming <figure>+<figcaption>. Deferred: client-side search, reading-time, manual dark toggle.",
      "rationale": "Distilled from reference blogs the user shared; all are static-friendly (zero or trivial JS) and fit 'keep it simple'. Newsletter is just a link to an external service (Buttondown/Substack) — no backend, consistent with comments being a non-goal.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Include client-side search now (needs JS + build index)",
        "Reading-time + manual theme toggle now"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D13",
      "timestamp": "2026-08-03",
      "phase": "4-feature-iteration",
      "decision": "Genie Mode (dev-only design cockpit): theme + limited config (lede/tagline/logo + hero background); Ollama with deterministic fallbacks; gitignored .filepress-genie/ versions; activate overwrites working tree; floating drawer; live inspire crawl; Openverse + local image upload; detect Ollama and suggest Finetuna (https://github.com/Catalyst-Forge-LLC/finetuna) for tuned local models. Never ships in preview/production.",
      "rationale": "Gives authors a post-import taste loop without becoming a CMS; keeps Markdown sacred and bake artifacts as plain theme.css/static/config. Finetuna is companion tooling (same org), not a hard dependency.",
      "alternatives_considered": [
        "Assistant Mode / Design Mode / Studio naming",
        "Theme-only mutation",
        "Deterministic-first without Ollama",
        "Commit-friendly version store",
        "Openverse-only images without upload"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D14",
      "timestamp": "2026-08-11",
      "phase": "4-feature-iteration",
      "decision": "Product name FilePress; npm package + planned domain getfilepress; GitHub/folder/CLI primary bin filepress (alias getfilepress). Scoped workspace packages @filepress/*; config defineFilepressConfig + filepress.config.ts. Formerly Downpress.",
      "rationale": "Bare npm name filepress rejected (too similar to vitepress). getfilepress stakes the package/domain while product branding stays FilePress. GitHub repo kept as filepress for short clone paths and github:Catalyst-Forge-LLC/filepress#… pins.",
      "alternatives_considered": [

        "Keep Downpress name"
      ],
      "status": "active"
    },

      "rationale": "Dogfood FilePress for the product site without a sibling-repo split yet; keep demo free of marketing copy so root pnpm check/build stay stable.",
